symptoms.title: No supported disease pattern
symptoms.description: The image did not show a strong pattern for Black Sigatoka, Panama Disease, or Cordana Leaf Spot. This is not proof that the whole plant is disease-free.

symptoms.title: Inspect the whole plant
symptoms.description: Check both leaf surfaces, older and younger leaves, the pseudostem, and the plant base for yellowing, spots, wilting, splitting, or internal discoloration.

symptoms.title: Watch for changes
symptoms.description: Symptoms can be absent or subtle in an early infection. Compare the plant over time and scan a clear, well-lit image of any new symptom.

treatment.title: Do not treat from this result alone
treatment.description: Do not apply a pesticide to a plant that appears healthy solely because of an app result. Use a confirmed diagnosis before treatment.

treatment.title: Continue appropriate care
treatment.description: Maintain suitable watering, drainage, nutrition, spacing, and sanitation for the banana variety and local conditions.

treatment.title: Ask an expert if concerned
treatment.description: If wilting, spreading lesions, or internal discoloration is present despite this result, contact a local agriculture or plant-health specialist.

prevention.title: Inspect plants regularly
prevention.description: Check leaves and pseudostems routinely so a new or changing symptom is noticed early.

prevention.title: Practice clean biosecurity
prevention.description: Use clean tools and footwear, avoid moving soil from diseased areas, and use healthy planting material from a reliable source.

prevention.title: Reduce plant stress
prevention.description: Provide balanced nutrition and appropriate water while preventing waterlogging, drought stress, crowding, and unnecessary leaf injury.
